course_description:
This course builds on the knowledge acquired in MUSC3840 Multi-Instrumental Pedagogy 1. Through lectures and specialised, practical Strings or Band streams, students will explore contemporary instrumental music pedagogy, learn instrument-specific skills, and build curriculum-aligned resources to support their future teaching goals.

Students will elect one instrument from MUSC3840 to continue, on which they will further develop their skills, aligning their learning with Curriculum Levels 3 and 4 of the Education Queensland Instrumental Music Curriculum. Additionally, students will learn one new instrument in the same stream (Strings or Band), aligning with Levels 1 and 2. Learning in a group context will be modelled throughout the course. Additionally, students will engage in workshopped teaching practice, ensemble playing and peer learning.

Instrument Allocation and Access

Students will continue with one instrument from MUSC3840 and one new instrument in the same stream (Strings or Band). Students are responsible for sourcing appropriate instruments (by borrowing, hiring, or purchasing) for the duration of this course. Please note that the university does not provide assistance with acquiring instruments.

All students who enrol in this course are required to complete an Instrument nomination form posted in Blackboard by the start of Orientation Week.

Ensemble Participation

All students are strongly encouraged to participate in an ensemble that aligns with their principal instrument or voice. Enrolment in separate Ensemble Studies courses is not required.

course_aims: The aim of this course is to deepen knowledge and skills for delivering instrumental training in educational contexts. This course will:

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate developing intermediate-level performance skills on one continuing instrument and functional beginner-level skills on a second instrument.
Design and implement effective instructional approaches aligned with contemporary pedagogical approaches and the Education Queensland Instrumental Music Curriculum.
Identify technical and musical issues in beginner performers and propose appropriate pedagogical interventions.
Critically reflect on personal teaching practice and justify pedagogical decisions.

assessment_details.title: Annotated Group Teaching Video
assessment_details.task_description: In this task, you will plan and teach one 20min lesson with a mixed instrument group of players from our class who will be playing one of the instruments they are studying as part of this course. Groups will be assigned by the tutor in your specialisation area. The teaching will happen outside of class, at a mutually agreed-upon time and location. You will record your teaching, then annotate it using EchoVideo to identify and justify the teaching strategies used, analyse their effectiveness, and cite learner outcomes and other observations. assessment_details.title: Final Performance
assessment_details.task_description: In this task, you will demonstrate your performance skills on the two instruments you have studied this semester. Your performance on Instrument A should demonstrate skills aligned with the Education Queensland Instrumental Music Curriculum Level 4, while your performance on Instrument B should align with Level 2. Your performance may include scales, technical exercises and solo repertoire, and may be sourced from the class method book or other appropriate sources (copies of other music should be provided). You are required to justify your selection of each scale/exercise/piece in your video prior to playing, aligning it to the appropriate curriculum level.
